title: Efficacy of severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome vaccines in animal models: a systematic review and meta-analysis

analysis.scope_and_question: Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS) is an emerging tick-borne zoonosis that threatens both animal and human health across East Asia, yet no licensed vaccine is currently available.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: We therefore conducted a PRISMA-guided systematic review and meta-analysis of preclinical murine and ferret studies to evaluate severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome virus vaccine efficacy. Seven electronic databases were searched for studies published between 2009 and 2025. Random-effects meta-analyses evaluated mortality, viremia, and post-challenge weight loss. Quantitative viral burden was further evaluated using standardized mean differences for mean and peak viremia, whereas body-weight trajectories were assessed using generalized linear mixed models.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Vaccination markedly reduced mortality (RR = 0.10, 95% CI 0.05–0.21), post-challenge weight loss (RR = 0.21, 95% CI 0.12–0.37), and detectable viremia (RR = 0.45, 95% CI 0.27–0.73), although the effect estimate was attenuated in the trim-and-fill sensitivity analysis (RR = 0.74, 95% CI: 0.36–1.51). Longitudinal analyses further demonstrated improved preservation of body weight, particularly following mRNA and vector vaccination.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The effect estimate was attenuated in the trim-and-fill sensitivity analysis, indicating potential heterogeneity or publication bias. The review does not report on the effectiveness of vaccines in natural host populations or in field settings.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: These findings provide the strongest quantitative evidence supporting the development of broadly protective SFTSV vaccines for both human and veterinary use within a One Health framework.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluates the efficacy of severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome virus (SFTSV) vaccines in preclinical animal models. The review included 23 studies from seven databases, published between 2009 and 2025, and used random-effects meta-analyses to assess mortality, viremia, and post-challenge weight loss. Vaccination significantly reduced mortality (RR = 0.10, 95% CI 0.05–0.21), post-challenge weight loss (RR = 0.21, 95% CI 0.12–0.37), and detectable viremia (RR = 0.45, 95% CI 0.27–0.73), although the effect estimate was weakened in trim-and-fill sensitivity analysis. Longitudinal analyses showed improved body weight preservation, especially with mRNA and vector vaccines. The findings support the development of broadly protective SFTSV vaccines for human and veterinary use, emphasizing the need for further research in natural host populations and field settings.

title: Multisystem biomarker trajectories and early risk of clinically adjudicated cardiogenic shock in severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome

analysis.research_question_and_background: Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS) is associated with substantial mortality, and shock with cardiac involvement is an important contributor to fatal outcomes. However, biomarker correlates, temporal trajectories, and early warning signals of clinically adjudicated cardiogenic shock (CS) in SFTS remain incompletely defined.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We retrospectively analyzed 775 laboratory-confirmed SFTS patients admitted to Nanjing Second Hospital from April 2020 through December 2024. The requirement for informed consent was waived because of the retrospective design and anonymized data collection.
analysis.methods: Time to first clinically adjudicated CS after admission was analyzed using univariable Cox regression, least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO), and multivariable Cox regression. Dynamic trajectories of 6 key biomarkers over the first 14 days were assessed using locally estimated scatterplot smoothing, and restricted cubic spline models were used to characterize continuous exposure-response relationships.
analysis.main_results: Clinically adjudicated CS occurred in 143 patients (18.5%); among 164 in-hospital deaths, 99 (60.4%) occurred in patients with CS. Biomarker trajectory analyses showed sustained increases in inflammatory, cardiac, renal, and coagulation markers in patients who developed CS, whereas lipid markers showed a time-dependent decline.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: In SFTS, clinically adjudicated CS clusters early after admission and reflects multisystem dysregulation involving inflammatory, cardiac, renal, coagulation, and lipid pathways.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: A six-biomarker panel may support early recognition of high-risk patients and help define a clinically relevant surveillance window during the first week of hospitalization.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is retrospective, and external validation and more objective cardiac assessment are needed before routine implementation. The evidence is moderate due to the observational nature and potential for confounding factors.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the relationship between biomarker trajectories and the early risk of clinically adjudicated cardiogenic shock (CS) in patients with severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS). The research highlights that CS occurs predominantly within the first week of admission, with most events occurring by day 7. Key findings show that elevated levels of interleukin-6, N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide, urea, fibrin/fibrinogen degradation products, and triglycerides are independently associated with increased CS risk, while total cholesterol shows an inverse association. The study suggests that a six-biomarker panel could aid in identifying high-risk patients early, although further validation and objective cardiac assessments are required. The evidence is moderate due to the observational design and potential for confounding factors, and the study's limitations include the need for external validation and more precise cardiac evaluation.

title: Integrated proteomic and metabolomic profiling characterizes tryptophan metabolic disturbance associated with mortality in ICU-admitted SFTS patients

analysis.research_question_and_background: Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS), caused by Dabie bandavirus, is associated with high mortality among intensive care unit (ICU) patients; however, the integrated proteomic–metabolomic mechanisms underlying fatal outcomes remain poorly characterized.
